name: WATER II
question: In men with symptomatic BPH and 80–150 mL prostates, does Aquablation meet prespecified three-month safety and symptom improvement goals?

design.population: 101 men with LUTS attributed to BPH and 80–150 mL prostates were enrolled at 16 centers in Canada and the United States.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Trial Design and Participants, p 322; Results, p 323

verdictNote: Both prespecified three-month performance goals were met in 101 treated men.
takeaway: In 101 men with 80–150 mL prostates, Aquablation met both three-month performance goals: procedure-related safety events occurred in 45.5% against a 65% ceiling, and mean IPSS fell from 23.2 to 6.7, exceeding the 11-point improvement threshold.

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.citation: Desai M, Bidair M, Zorn KC, et al. "Aquablation for benign prostatic hyperplasia in large prostates (80–150 mL): 6-month results from the WATER II trial." *BJU Int.* 2019;124(2):321-328. doi:10.1111/bju.14703
reports.followUp: Primary safety and efficacy assessments at 3 months; additional outcomes through 6 months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, p 322; Results and Fig. 1, p 323

results.measure: Clavien–Dindo grade 2 or higher, or grade 1 causing persistent disability, through 3 months; prespecified ceiling 65%
results.note: Tested by exact binomial test against an external performance goal, without a concurrent TURP arm. The paper does not state the event numerator, analysis denominator, or a numerical confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Endpoints and Statistical Analysis, pp 322–323; Results, p 324

results.measure: Mean IPSS at baseline and 3 months; noninferiority to a 16-point reduction with a 5-point margin (reduction statistically greater than 11 points)

values.exp: 23.2 ± 6.3 at baseline (101 treated); 6.7 ± 5.1 at 3 months (98 attended visit)

results.note: The 16.5-point difference is subtraction of rounded reported means; the paper gives no numerical confidence interval or endpoint-specific measurement denominator.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Endpoints and Statistical Analysis, pp 322–323; Results and Fig. 1, pp 323–324

results.measure: Mean maximum flow at baseline and 6 months, mL/s
results.note: Six-month observation of a prespecified three-month secondary endpoint; difference calculated from reported means. A numerical confidence interval was not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Endpoints and Statistical Analysis, p 323; Results, p 323; Fig. 2, p 325

results.measure: Mean IPSS at baseline and 6 months; 98/101 completed the six-month visit
results.note: Reported paired mean improvement; rounded baseline and six-month means differ by 17.3 points. No numerical confidence interval or endpoint-specific measurement denominator was provided.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 323–324; Fig. 2, p 325

results.measure: Mean PVR at baseline and 6 months, mL
results.note: Six-month observation of a prespecified three-month secondary endpoint; no numerical confidence interval or endpoint-specific measurement denominator was provided.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Endpoints and Statistical Analysis, p 323; Results, p 323; Fig. 2, p 325

results.measure: Secondary procedure to remove additional prostate tissue through 6 months
results.note: Prespecified at three months; none occurred through six months.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Study Endpoints and Statistical Analysis, p 323; Results, p 324

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo events through 6 months
harms.note: Procedure/device-related events; patients can have more than one event or grade.

harms.label: Bleeding requiring intervention and/or transfusion

values.exp: 14/101 (13.9%) with bleeding events: 8/101 (7.9%) before discharge and 6/101 (5.9%) within one month after discharge; 8/101 (7.9%) received transfusion alone, 3/101 (3.0%) underwent fulguration alone, and 2/101 (2.0%) received both

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 324; Table 4, p 327
harms.note: Two patients had both transfusion and fulguration; the 14 bleeding cases include hematuria, clot retention and blood-loss anemia.

harms.label: Persistent grade 1 and other urinary adverse events

values.exp: persistent grade 1: 18/101 (17.8%), including ejaculatory dysfunction 13, incontinence 3, and both 2; UTI: 6/101 (5.9%); other infection: 2/101 (2.0%); grade 3 urinary retention: 1/101 (1.0%); grade 3 incontinence requiring artificial urinary sphincter: 1/101 (1.0%)

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 324; Table 3, p 326
harms.note: The five grade 1 incontinence events persisted at six months; the grade 3 stress-incontinence case was additional.

delivery.label: Hospital stay
delivery.value: Mean 1.6 days (range 0–6 days; N=100, one excluded for concurrent non-prostatic hospitalization)

delivery.label: Procedure and catheter duration
delivery.value: 101 treated: mean handpiece-in to catheter-in time 37 minutes (range 15–97), TRUS-in to catheter-in time 55 minutes, and waterjet resection time 8 minutes (range 3–17); mean postoperative catheter duration 94 hours (range 17–729), with 68% discharged with a catheter
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, pp 323–324; Table 2, p 324
delivery.note: The 37-minute and 55-minute measures have different start points.

reports.label: Final five-year follow-up
reports.citation: Bhojani N, Bidair M, Kramolowsky E, et al. "Aquablation Therapy in Large Prostates (80-150 mL) for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Due to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Final WATER II 5-Year Clinical Trial Results." *J Urol.* 2023;210(1):143-153. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000003483
reports.followUp: Five years; 60 of 101 completed the 60-month visit
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results, paragraph 1; Table 1 lists 62 available at 60 months

results.measure: Mean IPSS among participants with five-year measurements
results.note: Reported mean paired change; rounded group means differ by 15.8 points.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'For the patients who completed the 5-year visit'; Figure 2

results.measure: Mean maximum flow among participants with five-year measurements, mL/s
results.note: Reported mean paired change; rounded group means differ by 8.5 mL/s.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'For the patients who completed the 5-year visit'; Figure 2

results.note: Kaplan–Meier estimate and crude count have different denominators.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph beginning 'During the 5-year follow-up'

harms.label: Procedure-related sexual dysfunction at 6 months
harms.note: Reported rates; denominator for the ejaculatory-function analysis is not stated in that paragraph.

harms.label: Late bleeding and outlet complications

values.exp: no transfusion or fulguration after day 30 through month 60; no urethral stricture or meatal stenosis during follow-up

harms.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph preceding Table 2
harms.note: No bladder-neck contracture was reported among those seen at the five-year visit.

delivery.label: Image-guided waterjet technique
delivery.value: 24F transurethral handpiece; real-time transrectal ultrasound contouring; automated waterjet, usually two or more passes for large glands
delivery.locator: Full text, Trial Design and Participants, Aquablation procedure paragraph

delivery.label: Hemostasis
delivery.value: Foley balloon tamponade: bladder neck 98/101, fossa 3/101; 40–80 mL balloon, traction and continuous irrigation; no electrocautery
delivery.locator: Full text, Trial Design and Participants, post-Aquablation paragraph

delivery.label: Procedure time and passes
delivery.value: Mean operative time 55 minutes; waterjet treatment 8 minutes; mean 1.8 passes

relations.note: Same Aquablation program; WATER randomized 30–80 mL glands against TURP, whereas WATER II enrolled 80–150 mL glands without a comparator.
